👇
To bypass an HP printer block on non-branded cartridges, dismiss prompt messages like "OK" or "Continue" if they appear. Otherwise, perform a hard power reset, disable Cartridge Protection in the printer settings or HP Smart App, clean the metal contacts, or reinstall the third-party cartridges one at a time.

Troubleshooting Steps: Dismiss the message: Press OK, Continue, or No on the printer screen if the option is available; some models let you print after acknowledging the warning.

Power reset: Unplug the printer while it is turned on, wait 2 minutes, plug it back into a direct wall outlet, and turn it on.

Reinstall sequentially: Remove all cartridges, insert one third-party cartridge, turn the printer off and on, and add remaining cartridges one by one.Clean the contacts: Take out the cartridges and wipe the copper-colored electrical chips with a clean, lint-free cloth or cotton swab.

Disable Cartridge Protection: Go to the setup or preferences menu on your printer's display screen or via the HP Smart App and turn off Cartridge Protection or anti-fraud settings.

Turn off auto-updates: Prevent future lockouts by turning off automatic firmware updates in your printer settings or software companion.A visual guide showing how to change settings and handle hardware tricks to clear non-HP cartridge warnings:

I have a couple of HP printers and went through this issue. I had signed up for the instant ink plan until I became increasingly frustrated that the company, essentially, bricks your ink cartridges once you reach a certain page limit. The company already made its money from me on the product. To then require me to pay in perpetuity for the “right“ to use said product is outrageous. It is diabolical. The moment HP installs any kind of firmware update and attempts to claim/assert control over a product I purchased years ago is the very moment that I am no longer using HP printers. IT'S THE HP SOFTWARE.
It's running on the computer and communicating over the internet.  Using the software with one of the target printer will result in the printer being flagged and you'll then be "encouraged" to connect the printer to network . . .

That said, when/while using the HP app, some individuals inadvertently activate HP+ and or the HP subscription service.
HP+ offers extended warranty for a device and allows one to use web and cell phone integration; but it forces the use of HP ink forever.  The subscription service is a different plan that does allow one to opt out (*** after satisfying the minimum subscription period/requirements ***).

So, when you get an HP message on your screen, try to slow down and read it; hastily clicking "OK" might make it go away but it might come back to haunt you.
